changelog: THE SCORE IS IN. Table of War has music — seven beds and six layers that follow what is actually happening rather than looping underneath it. The title is low tribal war drums. The expedition map is sparse and searching, and it thickens as the run goes on: act II brings a plucked canon that never lines up, act III a wedge of strings closing in, act IV the march finally arriving right-way-up, each stacking on the last. BATTLE AND BOSS ARE OPPOSITES, NOT LOUD AND LOUDER. A battle drives at 135 on a marching snare; a boss is slower and carries its weight instead of its speed — no marching snare anywhere, timpani and low toms, tuba and contrabass underneath, about half as many notes. They sit one note apart, so they flow into each other but can never be mistaken for one another. As your HQ is ground down a desperate layer rises over either one; when a boss turns, his own layer comes in on top, and both can be true at once. THE CAMP AND THE OUTPOST NOW SOUND DIFFERENT. They used to share one track with the run summary. The camp is a low swing jazz trio, the outpost is brighter and quicker, and the summary keeps the bed it always had.
